Calculate Governance Scores

Source: R/get-scores.R
get_scores.Rd

Scores organizations on the nonprofit governance index. By default (model = "2023") the function applies the 2023 anchor model: a bifactor item response model fit to all 501(c)(3) full Form 990 filers in tax year 2023. It appends a general governance score, four specific-factor scores, and a simple count of practices. The original 2018 six-factor model remains available as model = "legacy-2018".

Usage

get_scores(
  feature.matrix,
  model = c("2023", "legacy-2018"),
  missing = TRUE,
  impute = "median",
  scores.by.hand = FALSE
)

Arguments

feature.matrix

A data.frame of features, the output of get_features. For model = "2023" it must contain the 16 GI_* item columns; for model = "legacy-2018" the 12 legacy features ("P12_LINE_1", "P4_LINE_12", ...).

model

Which scoring model to apply: "2023" (default) or "legacy-2018".

missing, impute, scores.by.hand

Used only by model = "legacy-2018"; passed to psych::factor.scores as in earlier versions. With missing = FALSE, rows with NA features are dropped.

Value

The input data frame with appended columns.

For model = "2023":

gov_score

General governance score (EAP estimate of the general factor). On the latent scale, 2023 501(c)(3) filers have mean 0 and SD 1. Higher means more of the recommended practices.

gov_score_se

Standard error of gov_score.

gov_s_finance, gov_s_minutes, gov_s_policy, gov_s_comp

Specific-factor scores for financial assurance, meeting minutes, written policies, and compensation process. These are residual dimensions, orthogonal to gov_score: a positive value means the organization does more in that area than its general score predicts. They are not standalone subscales, and they are much less reliable than gov_score (empirical reliability among 2023 filers: finance .57, compensation .48, minutes .41, policy .29, vs .83 for gov_score). Only gov_s_finance carries substantial variance of its own. Do not use gov_s_policy: the written-policy items are the core of gov_score, and the policy factor has almost no variance of its own (omega-hierarchical < .01); it only contrasts the conflict-of-interest items with the whistleblower and retention policies. It is returned for completeness.

gov_count

Number of the 16 practices present (0–16), a transparent alternative that correlates about .96 with gov_score.

gov_n_items

Number of the 16 items answered. Rows with no answered items get NA scores.

For model = "legacy-2018": six factor scores and total.score, as in earlier versions of the package.

Details

2023 model. The model has a general factor and four specific factors (testlets) that absorb the strong dependence among nested items:

  • financial assurance: review/audit, audit, audit committee, accrual;

  • minutes: board and committee minutes;

  • written policies: conflict-of-interest policy, disclosure, monitoring, whistleblower, retention;

  • compensation: CEO and other-officer pay process.

Board independence, Form 990 review by the board, and posting the 990 online load on the general factor only. Item parameters are fixed at their 2023 values (gov_model_2023), so scores for other tax years are on the 2023 scale and can be compared over time; the items show no meaningful differential functioning across tax years 2021–2024. Missing items are handled by the IRT model (scores use the answered items). Scores are expected a posteriori (EAP) estimates computed with mirt::fscores.

Three financial-assurance items (audit, review or audit, accrual) show moderate differential item functioning by organization size: at the same general level, larger organizations are more likely to be audited, in part because of legal and funder audit thresholds. Keep this in mind when comparing organizations of very different size.

Legacy model. The 2018 model has known problems, including negative implied weights on several good-practice features and a training sample that excluded fully independent boards. It is kept for reproducing earlier work. See "Known issues" in vignette("legacy-2018-model", package = "governance").

See also

get_features, gov_model_2023.

Examples

data("dat_example", package = "governance")
set.seed(57)
dat_example <- dat_example[sample(seq_len(nrow(dat_example)), 200), ]
features_example <- get_features(dat_example)

# 2023 index (default)
scores_example <- get_scores(features_example)
summary(scores_example$gov_score)
#>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max. 
#> -1.944843 -0.847470  0.006912  0.007729  0.754730  1.692339 

# legacy 2018 model
legacy <- get_scores(features_example, model = "legacy-2018")
